In 2018, DTP1 coverage ranged from 84% in the African Region to 97% in the European Region.
Among the 19.4 million children who failed to receive DTP3 in 2018, 11.7 million (60%) lived in 10 countries
Global coverage with the third dose of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and pertussis-containing vaccine has not increased above 86% since 2010.
DTP1-to-DTP3 dropout rates were highest (7%) among low-income countries and lowest among high-income countries (3%).
Overall, 129 (66%) of the 194 WHO member countries achieved ≥90% national DTP3 coverage in 2018, up from 123 (63%) countries in 2017
Coverage varies across regions and countries, with lower coverage in lower-income countries.

equity.level_reason: Groups compared are WHO regions and country income or Gavi groups, which are geography rather than SPDs; equity is raised only as a recommendation (equitable access). Age only defines the population.

level_alternative.reason: The equity mention is a generic recommendation about country settings, not about any social-position group, so it may not count even as level 1.

ev.q: DTP3 coverage by age 12 months is a principal indicator of immunization program performance.

equity.equity_measurement: Countries are grouped by WHO region, World Bank income classification and Gavi eligibility (country-level geography and income groups, not SPDs); no within-country SPD breakdowns.

notes: The report summarizes and aggregates WHO/UNICEF national coverage estimates; dropout and between-vaccine differences are arithmetic, so no procedures are recorded. Vaccine-dose differences computed within regions and income groups were read as comparisons, not stratification. Designs are inferred; none is named.
view_issues: Article notes a post-publication correction (erratum 2019-11-08); the corrected values are not identified in the text.
